newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, market quiet.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, market quiet.

text.p: German call money was little changed on Tuesday, trading in a wide range of three to 3.10 percent, in a quiet, unruffled market.

Traders said the market remained adequately supplied with liquidity. They expected an expiring repo pact worth 78.1 billion marks to be more or less fully replaced in a new allocation of liquidity to the market tomorrow.

Banks held 40.5 billion marks of reserves at the Bundesbank on Monday for an avverage of 40.8 billion for the first six days of the month. Banks took up around 100 million marks at the 4.50 percent Lombard rate.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average was calculated at 3.09925 percent compared with 3.10333 percent on Monday.
